sections.h2: What should a seller know about Beavercreek, Ohio?
sections.html:
Beavercreek is the largest city in Greene County and sits about five miles east of downtown Dayton, which puts a large share of the Dayton area's homes within reach of buyers who work in the city. The Census Bureau estimated the 2025 population at 48,134, and the city covers about 26.6 square miles of land.

The area was settled in the early 1800s, and part of Beavercreek Township incorporated as a city in February 1980. The city absorbed the former communities of Alpha, Knollwood, most of New Germany and Zimmerman, and an older deed may use one of those names. The legal description and parcel number in your deed matter more to a title company than the neighborhood label.

sections.h2: How do Beavercreek housing numbers compare with the rest of the area?
sections.html:
Beavercreek has more renters than the lakeshore suburbs of Lorain County. QuickFacts lists a 2020 to 2024 owner-occupied rate of 71.8%, a median owner-occupied value of $279,600 and a median gross rent of $1,457. The city counts 19,453 households at 2.39 people each, and median monthly owner costs are $1,837 with a mortgage and $838 without.

  • The 2020 census counted 19,980 housing units, with 5.3% vacant.
  • Of the occupied units, 72.6% were owner-occupied and 27.4% were rented.
  • The median age was 40.6, and 20.0% of residents were 65 or older.

A rental share of more than a quarter of occupied homes means landlords and renters make up part of the demand. A homeowner with a long repair list can ask a direct buyer about an as-is purchase instead of renovating first.

sections.h2: Which Beavercreek permits and registrations come up at sale?
sections.html:
Beavercreek splits permits between the city and the county. The city's Planning and Development Department issues zoning permits, while Greene County Building Regulation handles building, plumbing, electrical and HVAC permits. The table lists the permit the city names for common projects, which helps you spot open work before a buyer's inspector does.

Permit that Beavercreek lists for common residential projects
ProjectPermit or office
New house, addition or attached garageResidential Zoning Permit
DeckResidential Zoning Permit
Swimming poolSwimming Pool Permit
Shed or detached garage, propane tankAccessory Structure Permit
Fence or retaining wallFence Permit
Interior remodel such as wall removal or a finished basementGreene County Building Regulation, no zoning permit
Abandoned, foreclosure or vacant propertyRegistration Application

Sources: beavercreekohio.gov.

The city says zoning permits are not required for interior remodeling, at-grade patios, garage sales or driveways. Applications run through the online permit center, and printed forms can be filed at City Hall on Research Park Drive. If the house is vacant, ask the planning office whether the registration rule applies to it.

sections.h2: Are short-term rentals allowed in Beavercreek?
sections.html:
Yes, with a city license. Ordinance 23-15 and Chapter 117 of the city code require every owner to apply through the Online Permit Center before operating a rental of less than thirty consecutive days. A license lasts two years and must be renewed.

  • The application lists the location, where the unit will be advertised, bedrooms, maximum occupants, parking and emergency contacts.
  • Renters must be at least 25 years old, and owners must give them house rules, noise rules and emergency details.
  • The city's 3% hotel, motel and short-term rental tax is filed quarterly, even for quarters with no rentals.

Owners inside a homeowners association should check its covenants first, as the city advises. If you are selling a house that has operated as a rental, tell buyers about the license and the tax filings, and ask the planning office whether a new owner must apply for a fresh license.

sections.h2: How does Greene County process a Beavercreek deed?
sections.html:
The Greene County Auditor transfers the deed, then the recorder files it. The auditor's page requires a completed Real Property Conveyance Statement of Value and Receipt (form DTE 100), and the name of the grantor must match how the grantor took title in the previous deed. The county map department must approve the deed before it reaches the auditor, and a property in the farmland tax program needs the DTE 101 statement.

The auditor's page prints the fee this way: a transfer tax of fifty cents per parcel and a conveyance fee of $2 for every thousand dollars of the sale price, rounded up to the nearest $100. The county has an online calculator for it. The deed also needs a complete legal description with the parcel number, a prepared-by statement, the prior deed reference and a notarial acknowledgment, which matches the signing rule in ORC 5301.01. The recorder's office files the deed afterward, and under ORC 5301.25 an unrecorded deed is treated as fraudulent against a later buyer who has no knowledge of it.

sections.h2: How are Greene County property taxes handled for a sale?
sections.html:
The county auditor appraises each parcel at fair market value every six years and updates values every three years. The auditor's office is at 69 Greene Street in Xenia, and its appraisers will talk through a valuation or start an appeal. Property tax dollars fund schools, safety services, roads, libraries and parks.

The treasurer's due dates move with state changes. For the second half of 2026, the Greene County Treasurer announced that the House Bill 186 inflation cap credit delayed bills, and that the state's Tax Commissioner approved a payment due date of Friday, August 14, 2026. Escrow borrowers needed to take no action. Ask the treasurer for the dates for your own closing year, and have the title company prorate taxes between you and the buyer.

sections.h2: What do Beavercreek schools, parks and transit mean for buyers?
sections.html:
Beavercreek City School District has one preschool, six elementary schools, two middle schools, a Freshman School and Beavercreek High School. The city parks department maintains 24 parks and properties, and Beavercreek Station is a hub on Creekside Trail, which runs from Xenia to Eastwood MetroPark in Dayton. The Greater Dayton Regional Transit Authority runs bus service in the city, and the public library is a branch of the Greene County Public Library.

These details help a listing, and they also help a direct buyer decide what the house is worth to the next owner. If you sell as is, ask the buyer to state in writing that repairs are theirs, and keep a copy of any inspection report you ordered.

faqs.q: Do I need a city permit to sell a house in Beavercreek?
faqs.a: The city's permit list covers construction work, short-term rental licenses and registration of vacant or foreclosure properties. Check for open permits on past work, since decks, pools, fences and sheds need zoning permits and the county handles building, plumbing, electrical and HVAC permits.

faqs.q: What fees does Greene County charge on a deed?
faqs.a: The auditor's page lists a transfer tax of fifty cents per parcel and a conveyance fee of $2 per thousand dollars of the sale price, rounded up to the nearest $100. The county's online calculator shows the amount for your sale.

faqs.q: Can a Beavercreek short-term rental license transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: Ask the planning office. Licenses last two years and are issued to the owner who applies, so a new owner may need to file a new application through the Online Permit Center.

faqs.q: When are Greene County taxes due?
faqs.a: Dates are set each year. The second half of 2026 was due Friday, August 14, 2026, after a delay tied to House Bill 186. Ask the Greene County Treasurer for the schedule that applies to your closing.

faqs.q: What must I disclose when I sell my Beavercreek home?
faqs.a: Use the Ohio property disclosure form for one to four unit homes. ORC 5302.30 lists exceptions such as estate sales and transfers to relatives, and a buyer who gets the form late may rescind within three business days.
